disease_sections.title: Obesity
disease_sections.overview: Obesity is a chronic condition characterized by excessive body fat accumulation that can affect overall health. It may result from genetic, lifestyle, environmental, and metabolic factors, and can increase the risk of conditions such as diabetes, heart disease, and hypertension.

current_status.clinical_warning: Seek medical support if obesity-related complications or difficulty losing weight persist.

Monitor weight and waist.
Check blood pressure, HbA1c, and lipids.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: A coordinated lifestyle plan can improve weight, fitness, and metabolic health.

disease_sections.title: NAFLD
disease_sections.overview: Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) is a condition where excess fat builds up in the liver in people who drink little or no alcohol, commonly linked to obesity, diabetes, and metabolic syndrome. If left untreated, it can progress from simple fatty liver to inflammation, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and even liver failure.

current_status.interpretation: Your results suggest significant liver fat requiring structured medical follow-up. Healthy lifestyle changes can still reverse much of the liver fat.
current_status.clinical_warning: Prompt follow-up with your doctor is recommended.

tips: Aim for about 10% weight loss with medical guidance.
Avoid sugary drinks and added sugars.
Follow regular aerobic and strength training.
exercise: Build toward 300 minutes of aerobic exercise weekly.

recommendations: Maintain a Mediterranean-style diet.
Eliminate fructose-rich drinks and added sugars.
Eat more vegetables, legumes, and whole grains.
Monitor liver enzymes, FIB-4, and FibroScan.
Repeat liver assessment every 3–6 months.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Your liver can recover significantly with consistent healthy choices.

disease_sections.title: Oxidative Stress
disease_sections.overview: Oxidative stress occurs when harmful free radicals outweigh the body's antioxidant defenses, leading to gradual damage of cells and tissues. Over time, this imbalance may contribute to aging and increase the risk of several chronic diseases.

current_status.interpretation: Your score reflects a moderate increase in oxidative stress. A structured lifestyle approach can still substantially lower risk.
current_status.clinical_warning: Medical review is recommended if metabolic abnormalities or persistent symptoms occur.

Monitor blood pressure, glucose, lipids, weight, and waist circumference.
Repeat abnormal tests as advised.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Improving daily habits can significantly reduce oxidative stress.

disease_sections.title: Hypertension
disease_sections.overview: Hypertension is a condition in which blood pressure remains consistently higher than normal, placing increased strain on the heart and blood vessels. Uncontrolled hypertension can cause organ damage over time and increase the risk of heart disease, stroke, and kidney issues.

current_status.interpretation: Your profile suggests an increased risk of developing hypertension. Early lifestyle changes can help improve blood pressure and reduce future cardiovascular risk.

disease_sections.title: Type 2 diabetes
disease_sections.overview: Type 2 diabetes is a metabolic disorder in which the body becomes resistant to insulin or does not produce enough insulin to maintain healthy blood sugar levels. Persistently elevated blood glucose can damage the eyes, kidneys, nerves, heart, and blood vessels over time.

current_status.interpretation: Early insulin resistance is developing, but this stage responds very well to lifestyle changes. Improving weight, activity, and diet can restore healthy blood sugar control.
current_status.clinical_warning: Discuss preventive management with your doctor. This is not an emergency.

tips: Lose around 5% body weight if overweight.
Exercise most days with cardio and strength training.
Avoid sugary drinks and refined carbohydrates.

recommendations: Choose a high-fibre, low-glycaemic diet.
Eat more legumes, vegetables, and whole grains.
Pair carbohydrates with protein or healthy fats.
Repeat HbA1c and fasting glucose in 6–12 months.
Monitor weight, waist circumference, blood pressure, and cholesterol.

disease_sections.positive_takeaway: Early insulin resistance is highly reversible with consistent lifestyle changes.
